newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended higher after a roller coaster ride on Thursday, with some dealers speculating on a rate cu, though generally ruled out by analysts, at Friday's Bank of Spain repurchase tender.
"I think tomorrow the Bank of Spain will cut the official rate by 25 basis points," said Emilio Sainz at Natwest in Madrid. "And if this happens, the market will reach a new high."

A Reuter survey of 10 analysts conducted before a Bank of Spain governor's speech showed no one expected a rate cut before November CPI data was out. But Luis Angel Rojo's remarks fuelled expectations of an upcoming cut in the key money market rate.
Earlier on Thursday, Rojo said inflation could end the year at 3.3 percent, below original expectations for 3.5 percent.

"I'm still convinced the Bank of Spain would rather wait, although a reduction in the rate is a real possibility," said Jose Ramon Nunez at Benito y Monjardin. December 13 was considered more likely for a rate cut because November inflation data would be announced.

The 10-year spread over the German Bunds, which had bounced back above 140 basis points earlier after dipping to a record low at 131 basis points on Wednesday, was trading at 135 basis points at the close.
